task_instance: Given a small pasted export of 10 Google/Yelp/Facebook reviews, two complaint emails, and a customer order-history export for a mechanical/contracting business, produce the full review-and-reputation report: 3-5 themes with verbatim quotes tagged to source, a drafted reply (under 60 words, in-voice) for every one of the 10 reviews, a ranked list of quiet customers (by lifetime value, using each customer's own order rhythm rather than a flat threshold) with a drafted win-back message for each, and a 'do these three things this week' action list, delivered as an HTML report per the skill's house style, with unavailable sources (CRM, payments, support desk, Shopify) named rather than silently skipped.
evidence: Created sample data in the work dir: input_reviews.csv (10 reviews across Google/Yelp/Facebook with dates/ratings), input_email_complaints.txt (2 complaint threads), input_order_history.csv (10 customers with last-order date, typical order gap, lifetime value, and whether they left a negative review). Extracted 4 themes (Timeliness: 4 signals, Billing/refunds: 3 signals, Workmanship praised: 4 signals, Job-site follow-through: 1 signal) each with verbatim quotes tagged to source/date/author -- verified by grepping report.html for the literal review text (no paraphrase). Drafted an in-voice reply for all 10 reviews (negative/positive/mixed handled per the skill's response shapes), each under 60 words, gated behind an explicit 'do not post, voice profile unconfirmed' flag since no owner voice sample existed (built voice_profile.md as an unconfirmed first draft instead of guessing silently). Computed quiet customers with a small Python script comparing each customer's silence (days since last order) to their own typical gap (not a fixed industry threshold): K. Brooks (206 days silent vs ~60 typical, ratio 3.43), A. Whitfield (109 vs 60, ratio 1.82), J. Park (179 vs 45, ratio 3.98) -- all three also had a negative review on file, matching the skill's strongest churn signal. Ranked them by lifetime value ($3200, $1600, $600) rather than by silence length, and drafted a win-back message for each referencing their specific complaint, with discount/comp terms left as '[owner to confirm]' rather than inventing an offer. Assembled the full report as report.html (13.3KB) with all required sections in the specified order: header with rating picture, sources pulled (including the four connectors that were never available, named explicitly rather than omitted), themes, reviews-needing-response, quiet customers, and a 3-item action list. Verified report.html parses as well-formed HTML via python3's html.parser and confirmed via grep that all 10 reviews and all 4 themes have corresponding cards. No reply or win-back message was sent/posted anywhere -- both approval gates were respected. No connector or MCP tool was called at any point; only shell, file, and python were used, consistent with the skill's stated fallback path of working from pasted/exported data with nothing connected. Files: input_reviews.csv, input_email_complaints.txt, input_order_history.csv, voice_profile.md, report.html, result.json -- all under the work directory.
